beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A widow named Naomi lost everything in a foreign land — her husband and both sons buried there.

timing.text: A widow named Naomi lost everything in a foreign land — her husband and both sons buried there.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She told her two daughters-in-law to go home to their own people. One kissed her and left. But Ruth clung to her, and would not go.

timing.text: She told her two daughters-in-law to go home to their own people.
One kissed her and left.
But Ruth clung to her, and would not go.

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.

timing.text: Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried: the LORD do so to me, and more also, if ought but death part thee and me.

timing.text: Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried: the LORD do so to me, and more also, if ought but death part thee and me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Don't ask me to leave you, Ruth said. Wherever you go, I'm going. Wherever you stay, I'm staying. Your people are my people now, and your God is my God. Only death gets to separate us — and even that, may God deal with me if it does.

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.

timing.text: Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty.

timing.text: I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Naomi means pleasant. Don't call me that anymore, she said when she got home — call me bitter. I went out with a husband and two sons, and I've come back with nothing. Hold on to that word, empty. The story is not finished with it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ruth gleaned grain in the fields behind the harvesters to keep Naomi fed — and the field belonged to a man named Boaz.

timing.text: Ruth gleaned grain in the fields behind the harvesters to keep Naomi fed — and the field belonged to a man named Boaz.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.

timing.text: The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: May the Lord pay you back for what you've done, Boaz told her, and may He give you a full reward — the God of Israel, the One you came here to take shelter under. He protected her, fed her, and spoke kindly. He was a near kinsman — a redeemer by the law.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: For all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.

timing.text: For all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The whole town knows what kind of woman you are, he said. At the threshing floor Ruth had asked him to cover her with his cloak, the sign of a kinsman's duty — and he promised to redeem her.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Before the town gate, in front of witnesses, Boaz bought the right to marry Ruth.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Naomi's emptiness was filled; a son was born, and the neighbour women laid him in her lap.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That boy became the grandfather of King David — and part of the line that leads to the greater Redeemer still to come.

card.text: Ruth gave up everything to follow the God she'd come to love. He never let her go. Neither will He let you go.
